speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and the timing of these movements relative to starting risperidone for schizophrenia, I suspect drug-induced parkinsonism, but I need to confirm the specific characteristics. Do you experience a "pill-rolling" tremor in your hands, or is the stiffness and shuffling gait the primary issues? Also, have you noticed any masking of the movements when you are concentrating, or are they constant?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone therapy. The combination of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still is classic for this extrapyramidal side effect, which occurs in approximately 10-20% of patients on first-generation or high-potency second-generation antipsychotics like risperidone. We should consider reducing the risperidone dose or adding a beta-blocker such as propranolol to manage these symptoms.
